phrases.english: Grandma gathered the olives into a basket
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

phrases.english: Let’s pick some flowers for Mummy.

phrases.latin: quō dum Prōserpina lūcō lūdit et aut violās aut candida līlia carpit
phrases.english: while Proserpina was playing in this grove, picking violets or white lilies

phrases.latin: sī flōrem acerbumve pirum aliudve quid dēcerpseris, in eōdem locō eōdem annō nihil renāscitur
phrases.english: if you pick a blossom or an unripe pear or anything else, nothing grows again in that place the same year
Pick the red tomatoes; leave the green ones.

phrases.latin: Māla mātūra carpāmus; tū corbem tenē.
phrases.english: Let’s pick the ripe apples; you hold the basket.

phrases.latin: Prīmus vēre rosam atque autumnō carpere pōma
phrases.english: the first to pick roses in spring and fruit in autumn (the old gardener of Corycus)

phrases.latin: ut gaudet īnsitīva dēcerpēns pira certantem et ūvam purpurae
phrases.english: how glad he is, picking the pears of his own grafting and the grapes that vie with purple

sources: Lewis & Short: carpo

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
